analysis.

A stack and a queue are both linear data structures, but they differ in the way elements are added and removed. 

In a stack, elements are added and removed from the same end, known as the top. This follows the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle. A real-world example of a stack is a stack of plates in a kitchen. When you add a plate, you place it on top of the stack, and when you remove a plate, you take it from the top.

In a queue, elements are added at one end (the rear) and removed from the other end (the front). This follows the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle. A real-world example of a queue is a line of people waiting at a ticket counter. The person who arrives first is served first, and new people join the end of the line.

This is my analysis.
